question: Simplify $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right)$.
explanation:
Using the half-angle identity $\tan\frac{x}{2}=\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}$.

Thus $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{x}{2}\right)=\frac{x}{2}$ in the principal domain.
